page: Microsoft Azure M16lds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel processor. It delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, provisioning 256.0 GB of system RAM, which provides 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware GPU acceleration is not included in this configuration.

Storage specifications include 591 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for temporary scratch space, swap, and high-throughput local caching operations. The instance also supports Azure Premium Storage for external managed disk attachments. Complimentary public IPv4 networking addresses are not included with the standard provisioning profile.

From an architectural standpoint, the M16lds_v4 prioritizes RAM density over sheer compute scale, improving cost efficiency for operations constrained by memory footprints rather than raw instruction throughput. Recommended workloads include large in-memory databases, relational database management systems, enterprise caching architectures, and memory-intensive analytics processing.
description: Microsoft Azure M16lds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Equipped with an Intel x86_64 architecture, the configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is bundled with 591 GB of local NVMe SSD ephemeral storage and supports Azure Premium Storage for external disk requirements. It does not incorporate hardware GPU acceleration and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its prominent memory footprint relative to CPU core count, the M16lds_v4 delivers resource density tailored to memory-heavy applications without incurring the cost of surplus compute capacity. Consequently, the virtual machine fits enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching servers, data analytics pipelines, and memory-bound transactional database environments.
